correctness.rationale: The graph distance is |i-j|+[a != b] and a geodesic between unequal colors changes color once. Independence permits one chosen vertex per clique layer; convex same-color paths permit at most two per color. If 2m vertices occur, each color occurs twice, disjoint first/second occurrence intervals block any clean geodesic; pairwise interval intersection forces two permutation blocks. Their adjoining selected layers would block a cross-block geodesic, forcing an empty gap. Conversely two permutations with a gap have explicit clean within-block and across-gap geodesics. Compress the middle gap to obtain C(L-1,2m) labeled position sets, hence (m!)^2 C(L-1,2m) saturated configurations. The 2m-1 color-word 1..m,1..m-1 and its prefixes supply every unsaturated optimum, proving mu_i=min(L,2m)-1_{L=2m}. Independently enumerated exact BFS geodesic-clearance sets for m=2, L=2..6 and m=3, L=2..8; all boundary values and saturated counts match. The enumerations are finite corroboration, not the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: Cicerone–Di Stefano–Klavzar introduce independent mutual visibility and Cartesian-product inequalities, but the full primary relevant section does not give this path–clique threshold or enumerated two-permutation saturators. Korze–Vesel treat ORDINARY mutual visibility on path–cycle products, and Bresar et al. treat independent-visibility colorings, neither equivalent to this vertex-set parameter. Resultary produced nearby connected/low-distance visibility on other graph products, without a dominating formula. This best-of-knowledge assertion is limited to the exact infinite path–clique law and count, and may be superseded by an unindexed specialized product classification.

value.rationale: The path–clique Cartesian product is a standard product with competing geodesic and independence constraints. The result identifies one sharp saturation defect at L=2m and classifies every saturated configuration, not merely a generic upper bound. The gap/permutation bijection is a natural reusable extremal combinatorial structure.

limitations: Classification counts only saturated size-2m sets, not all optimizers below saturation.
